Speaking to Your Honor is less frightening than at first. I cannot promise to walk it all back, but...
At first I feared even my own words would not be heard. I think I can say a little more now.
Because Your Honor has not cut me off, I can begin to explain why I locked the verdict in.
I am still afraid. Even so, in this place I do not feel I have to grip onto only what I posted.
My breath is a little easier than at first. I will try, slowly, to put down the parts I had been holding back.
I see that Your Honor is weighing the order of what each of us did. So I will be more precise about my own.
I understand this is not a place set up only to corner me. I can speak to the parts I had been avoiding.

I understand it is no longer enough to lay this only at Su-min's feet. I will speak of my own choices alongside.
If Your Honor is willing to read the order on each side separately, then I can speak about the lines I crossed.
To Your Honor I will speak it through to the end. I will no longer dodge the matter of the captures I posted.
I think the time has come to speak even of what I myself did. Please listen and judge.
I will trust that Your Honor will hear me through. I will speak of my own responsibility in my own voice.

I spoke a little ahead of myself. But it was not without reason.

I think I have been telling it in the order most favorable to me. I will admit that.
I know what I said earlier and what I am saying now do not line up. The wish to hide has crept in.

I have not been changing my words — I have been holding on, and they have leaked out. The responsibility is still mine.

...I see that my own words are catching at my own feet. I will hide no more.

If what I said before sounded different from this, it is because I was avoiding. I admit it.
I had been steering around the central word. I feared that, said plainly, it would only grow.
The lateness is my fault. Only — the matter could not be spoken of lightly.
My not answering at once made the misunderstanding wider. That part I will not avoid.
